title: Today's top defense-tech headlines
big: 53 new stories since the last brief. The busiest areas: allies & theaters and drones & air autonomy.

stories.h: U.S. Intel Warns China’s Space-Based Directed Energy Weapons Could Soon Threaten Satellites
stories.what: Battlefield space is heating up as the DIA warns that China could use orbital directed energy weapons to take down satellites by the end of the decade. The post U.S.
stories.you: More of the military's sensing and communications now runs through orbit, and new suppliers are getting in.

stories.h: Ukraine’s Linza bomber drone clears path for UGV in German exercise
stories.what: Ukrainian drone maker Frontline Robotics flew its Linza bomber drone alongside German, Ukrainian and other unmanned air, ground and sea systems during Forward Edge 26, a two-week exercise in Germany hosted by Quantum Systems, the company said on social media.
stories.you: Drones are becoming the military's default purchase, so volume, price and reliability decide who wins.

stories.h: ICAM, Cloud and AI: Five Insights Into the VA’s $10.7B FY27 IT Systems Budget
stories.what: Discover the essential technologies the VA seeks with its fiscal year 2027 healthcare IT systems and EHR budget request. The post ICAM, Cloud and AI: Five Insights Into the VA’s $10.7B FY27 IT Systems Budget first appeared on Executive Gov .
stories.you: Software that decides what to look at and what to hit is where the most value is moving.

stories.h: AUKUS partners test autonomous systems as Europe weighs maritime surveillance needs
stories.what: The UK headed up the anti-submarine warfare component of Maritime Big Play exercise, which took place off the coast of San Diego in October.
stories.you: The Navy is short of ships and is turning to cheaper unmanned boats, which opens the door to new builders.

stories.h: US, Japan ink agreements for AMRAAM assembly, SM-3 production boost: Japanese MoD
stories.what: The “groundbreaking agreement” on AMRAAM production “will not only ensure the acquisition of equipment needed by both Japan and the United States, but will also strengthen Japan’s defense industry base,” said Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi.
stories.you: Missile defense is one of the biggest budget lines this decade, and its software and sensors are open to newcomers.
